chunks: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Takbir (saying 'Allahu Akbar') is [required] in every obligatory [prayer], and there is no Takbir in the voluntary [prayers] during the days of Tashriq.

key_terms.أَيَّامَ التَّشْرِيقِ: The Days of Tashriq (11th-13th of Dhu al-Hijjah), specifically associated with Eid al-Adha rituals.
key_terms.التَّكْبِيرُ: The act of saying 'Allahu Akbar' (God is the Greatest), a ritual declaration.

ai.seo_question: Is the post-prayer Takbir obligatory for all prayers or only specific ones during Eid al-Adha?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the Takbir as a mandatory Sunnah specifically for the five daily Fard prayers during the Days of Tashriq, distinguishing it from Nafl prayers where it is not prescribed. This highlights the unique liturgical status of these days in Shia jurisprudence, where the remembrance of God is intensified immediately following obligatory acts to commemorate the completion of Hajj rituals.
